texts: Before elective CABG in a patient on aspirin and clopidogrel, stop clopidogrel 5 days before surgery and continue aspirin at the low dose of 81 mg.
Clopidogrel within 5 days of surgery clearly increases bleeding, transfusion and re-exploration.
Aspirin is continued because it lowers perioperative ischaemic events and protects the stent and the new grafts, and a low dose bleeds less than 325 mg.
His drug-eluting stent was placed 2 years ago, well past the period when stopping clopidogrel risks stent thrombosis.
Stopping both drugs exposes him to ischaemia, and 3 days off clopidogrel is not long enough.
In the picture, the man leaves his clogs by the door under the hamsa painting, and the big asp shrinks to a small asp that stays on.
Memory hook: clogs off five days before; the asp stays, small.
